note: Deepening pass on an already-published city (10 trees live). Source pool: the Comune di Milano's own monumental-tree pages, which publish one page per tree with address, description, the city's VTA inventory number, height, trunk diameter and a map point (13 trees), cross-read against the 33 MASAF national-register entries within 12 km of the Duomo. Five additions went to data/research/milan-extra.json; everything else is here. Counts to quote carefully: the comune publishes 13, the national register holds 22 for the comune of Milano and about 75 for the metropolitan area, and the two lists overlap without matching, because several nationally designated trees stand on state, church or university ground the city does not manage. Lombardia publishes no per-tree regional register: the only regional dataset is Bellezze Individue (SIBA landscape designations, CC0), which designates gardens and parks rather than individual trees, gives every Milano row the same comune-centroid coordinate, and carries no species, age or vitality field. The city's two labelled botanical trails (Parco Sempione, 31 plants; Giardino della Guastalla, 41) turn out to be species-teaching routes with no individual ages or measurements, so they are good for confirming a species on the spot and useless as a second source for a specific tree.

leads.name: Il bagolaro di Villa Marietti Radice Fossati
sources: MASAF national register, Villa Marietti Radice Fossati
leads.why_not_published: Verifies on two sources and has a genuinely good story (the comune retells the folk name Arcidiavolo and the legend that Lucifer carried the species to earth in his claws, which is why the leaves are hooked). Held back only because it stands alone: 4.7 km northwest of the Duomo, 2.5 km from the Villa Litta pair, so it joins no walk. Access also needs a sentence of care, since the villa is a lived-in residential community and the comune's own wording is that one may enter the gate 'with the discretion owed to an inhabited place'. Pick this up if Milan ever wants a northwestern point.

leads.name: Il platano di Viale Montesanto 4/6
sources: MASAF national register, Milano, Viale Montesanto 4/6
leads.why_not_published: Single-sourced and unnamed. At 38 m it is one of the tallest registered trees in Milan and it sits between Porta Garibaldi and the Montanelli gardens, so it would extend that walk northwest if a second source turns up.

leads.name: Il platano di Viale Vittorio Veneto 3
sources: MASAF national register, Milano, Viale Vittorio Veneto 3
leads.why_not_published: Single-sourced, unnamed, and a street tree on the Bastioni rather than a destination. Sits 300 m off the northeast corner of the Giardini Montanelli, so it is cheap to add to that walk the day a second source exists.

leads.name: Two further planes inside the Giardini Montanelli
sources: MASAF national register, Giardini Indro Montanelli (625 cm / 28 m at 45.473889, 9.200833 and 475 cm / 34 m at 45.474389, 9.203111)
leads.why_not_published: Single-sourced and unnamed. The comune publishes pages for only three Montanelli trees plus the bald cypress and the hackberry; these two are register rows with no municipal page, no name and no story, and the gardens already carry five of our entries. Raw material for a later depth pass, not page-worthy on their own. UPDATE 2026-08-08 verify pass: the 475cm/34m entry (45.474389,9.203111) now has a second source (Il Giorno, ilgiorno.it/milano/cronaca/alberi-monumentali-1.7590565, verbatim confirms a second 34m plane at Giardini Montanelli via Palestro) and has been promoted and delivered as mil_018 in data/research/milan-verified.json. The other row, 625cm/28m at (45.473889,9.200833), is STILL single-sourced (MASAF only); comune.milano.it is now returning 403 to every fetch (curl and WebFetch alike), so the comune-page route the earlier pass used to find second sources is currently closed. Remains a lead until a second source turns up.

leads.name: Il platano di Piazzale Libia
sources: MASAF national register, Milano, Piazzale Libia
leads.why_not_published: Single-sourced and unnamed, and 1 km east of the Porta Romana cluster on a large traffic circle. Would need a second source and a reason to walk there.

leads.name: Milan's other Villa Litta planes
sources: MASAF national register, Viale Affori - Villa Litta Modignani (550 cm / 43 m and 480 cm / 38 m, plus two entries with no girth at 30 m and 28 m)
leads.why_not_published: The register holds four Villa Litta plane entries and the comune publishes pages for two of them; only the Siamese survives the identification test cleanly. The 43 m specimen is the tallest registered tree in Milan and is almost certainly one of the surviving 18th-century planes a local history source describes as still standing 'oltre i trenta metri', but no source ties a name, a page or a photograph to a specific coordinate, and one of these four rows may well be the tree felled in 2015. Do not publish any of them until a site visit or a current municipal inventory says which is which.

leads.name: Monumental trees in the wider metropolitan area
sources: MASAF national register, comuni of Cinisello Balsamo, Pioltello, Bollate, Vimodrone
leads.why_not_published: Outside the day-trip boundary as walks, but on the record: a 495 cm hackberry in Vicolo Cornelio and a 445 cm hackberry plus a magnolia in the park of Villa Ghirlanda at Cinisello Balsamo (9 to 10 km), a hackberry-and-yew group in Piazza Giovanni XXIII at Pioltello (11 km), a 400 cm black poplar in Bollate, a magnolia at Villa Torri in Vimodrone. Candidate pool if Milan ever grows a second page or a Lombardy collection.

leads.name: Il platano di Viale Vittorio Veneto 3
sources: MASAF national register, Milano, Viale Vittorio Veneto 3
leads.why_not_published: CAUTION added 2026-08-08 verify pass, not resolved either way: still single-sourced (as the original 2026-08-05 pass found), and a genuine dead-tree risk has now surfaced. Urbanfile (blog.urbanfile.org/2018/07/10/milano-porta-venezia-rimosso-lalbero-ormai-secco-da-oltre-due-anni/, 10 July 2018) reports a large plane tree on Viale Vittorio Veneto near Porta Venezia that dried out completely by 2016 and was removed on 8 July 2018, trunk 'circa tre metri di circonferenza' (about 3 m girth), standing in the tram-line median. The register's tree is a different size (570 cm girth, nearly double), so this is very likely a DIFFERENT specimen still standing at house number 3, but the article gives no exact address to rule it out cleanly. Do not publish without either (a) a second source confirming this specific 570 cm tree is alive, or (b) ruling out that it is the felled one. A future pass should check satellite imagery or a recent street-level photo of Viale Vittorio Veneto 3 before doing anything else with this candidate.

blocked.name: Il platano del 1773 a Villa Litta
blocked.reason: Dead, and the register entry has outlived it. Local history source milanoaffori.it states the plane dated to 1773 stood on the southeast side of Villa Litta Modignani 'fino al 2015' and was then felled; the six-quintal trunk section that produced the 1773 ring count, El Rondelun, is displayed in the villa's civil wedding hall with a timeline panel running 1773 to 2015. The comune's own page still describes the tree in the present tense, with height, diameter, cabling and a fence, and dates it from a section it attributes to a lost twin. Both cannot be true. Our own city file already tells the felled version in its FAQ. A dendrochronologically dated tree is the best evidence this project ever gets and it is still not enough to publish a tree that a local source says has been gone for eleven years.

blocked.name: Il platano dei Giardini di Villa Belgiojoso (Villa Reale di Palestro)
sources: MASAF national register, Villa Belgioioso Bonaparte - Via Palestro 16
blocked.reason: Access-restricted, and enforced. The garden of Villa Belgiojoso Bonaparte admits children under 12; adults may enter only accompanying one, and the Guardie Ecologiche Volontarie check at the gate. A 35 m plane, one of the tallest trees in Milan, that most of our readers are not allowed to walk up to fails the promise the site makes. Revisit if the announced two-million-euro restoration opens the garden to visitors of the Galleria d'Arte Moderna, which the 2026 press coverage floats as a possibility.

blocked.name: Il bagolaro dei Giardini di Villa Belgiojoso (Villa Reale di Palestro)
sources: MASAF national register, Villa Belgioioso Bonaparte - Via Palestro 16
blocked.reason: Same closed gate as the plane above: adults only when accompanying a child under 12. Two further strikes even if it opened: the comune says this specimen is one of a pair growing into each other, so the point is not singular, and its measurements are nearly identical to the hackberry we already publish 200 m away in the Giardini Montanelli (mil_003), which the comune itself notes.

blocked.name: L'insieme omogeneo di Ginkgo biloba, Orto Botanico di Brera
sources: MASAF national register, Orto Botanico di Brera, Via Brera 28
blocked.reason: Not a separate tree. This is the register's group entry ('insieme omogeneo') covering the 1775 ginkgo pair we already publish as mil_004, which is why the register shows no girth or height for it. Recorded here so a future pass does not read it as an eleventh tree.

blocked.name: La Quercia di Montale
sources: milan.json FAQ, researched in an earlier pass
blocked.reason: Fallen. The red oak known as the Quercia di Montale came down in October 2019 in heavy rain and its trunk was left in place. Already handled honestly in the city page's FAQ; listed here so nobody re-researches it as a candidate.

blocked.name: 40 m Himalayan Cedar, Viale Cervantes, Parco Sempione (RAMI candidate, not MASAF)
sources: https://ilregistrodeglialberi.it/2279-cedro-parco-sempione-cedro-milano-mi-lombardia (RAMI, crowd-sourced, Oct 2021 survey: girth 380 cm, height 40 m, health 'Buona')
blocked.reason: NOT blocked outright, filed here as a flagged lead rather than a dead end: RAMI is a citizen/collaborative registry, not an official government register, so on its own it does not meet the two-independent-sources bar and it is not in our licensed MASAF import. No second source was found this pass. Separately, a 2019 MilanoToday user report (milanotoday.it/social/segnalazioni/abbattuto-albero-himalaya-sempione.html, 13 Nov 2019) describes a healthy Himalayan cedar felled in Parco Sempione and says 'non è il primo' (not the first); since RAMI's survey is dated Oct 2021, two years later, it is probably a different, still-living cedar, but this has not been confirmed. If a height of 40 m holds up, this would be one of the tallest trees in Milan and worth a dedicated look: try the comune's own Parco Sempione tree-walk PDF (yesmilano.it/system/files/itinerario/allegati/3752/12104/Parco%20Sempione-percorsi%20alberi-guida.pdf, not yet fetched this pass) as a possible second source.
